title: Bastar culture and heritage — overview
text: The official Bastar district Culture & Heritage page describes Bastar as a place with longstanding cultural traditions associated with forest-dwelling and tribal communities. It highlights Bastar Dussehra, memorial pillars, and the Ghotul tradition. The page was last updated on 25 September 2018, so descriptions should be treated as the district website's published account rather than a comprehensive or recently verified ethnographic source.

title: Bastar Dussehra — festival traditions
text: According to the official Bastar district Culture & Heritage page, Bastar Dussehra is distinctive because it is described as lasting around 75 days and does not include the burning of a Ravana effigy. The page says the festival begins with a ritual in which the first wood for a chariot is brought from the forest; this is called Pat Jatra. It concludes with Muria Durbar, described by the page as a gathering where the Maharaja's court listens to public concerns. This is the website's account, last updated 25 September 2018; dates and current festival arrangements should be checked with current official event notices.
category: Bastar Dussehra; festival; Pat Jatra; Muria Durbar

title: Bastar memorial pillars — Gudi tradition
text: The official Bastar district Culture & Heritage page describes a memorial custom known as a deceased or memorial pillar, particularly among Maria and Muria communities in southern Bastar. It says these pillars are called 'Gudi' in the local language and describes stone markers placed at ancestral burial locations. The source is a short district-webpage description last updated in 2018; terminology and community-specific details should be corroborated with local cultural experts or authoritative ethnographic sources before making broad claims.
category: tribal heritage; memorial pillars; Maria; Muria; Gudi

title: Ghotul tradition in Bastar
text: The official Bastar district Culture & Heritage page says the Ghotul tradition is associated with Madia communities in Bastar. It describes a village-edge mud structure used as a gathering place during festivals and notes that some structures have open floors or lack walls. The source's description is brief and dates to 2018. Avoid generalizing this account to all tribal communities or treating it as a full description of present-day practice.
category: Ghotul; community traditions; Madia; cultural heritage

title: Traditional handicrafts of Bastar
text: The official Bastar district Handicraft (Art and Culture) page groups traditional Bastar crafts into woodwork, bamboo art, soil/clay art, and metal arts. Examples described include wooden figures and decorations; bamboo chairs, baskets, mats and household items; clay figures, pots and decorative utensils; and metal objects such as deities, ritual figures and home furnishings. The page says these crafts use conventional tools and often reflect the rural life and cultural practices of local communities. Last updated 25 September 2018.
category: handicrafts; woodwork; bamboo; clay; metal craft

title: Dhokra and bell-metal craft in Bastar
text: The official Bastar district Handicraft page highlights Dhokra handicraft and bell-metal craft. It describes Dhokra materials as including cow dung, paddy husk, red soil and beeswax, with wax wires used for contours and decoration. It also notes that metal craft is used to make figures associated with worship, tribal culture and home decoration. This summary reflects the district website's description, last updated in 2018; specific technical details should be corroborated with craft practitioners or specialist sources.
category: Dhokra; bell metal; metal craft; artisan techniques

title: Data quality note — Bastar culture and handicrafts

title: Places of interest in Bastar — overview
text: The official Bastar district Places of Interest page describes the district as a destination known for forests, tribal culture, natural resources and handicrafts. It identifies Jagdalpur as the district headquarters and lists the Indravati River, Anthropological Museum at Dharampura, Bastar Palace, Bastar Dussehra, Dalpat Sagar, Chitrakote Waterfall, Tirathgarh Waterfall, Kotumsar Cave and Kailash Cave among notable attractions. The page gives the district area as 6,596.90 square kilometres. Tourism descriptions and distances on the page should be checked against current official guidance before travel.

title: Chitrakote Waterfall — Bastar
text: Chitrakote Waterfall is located on the Indravati River in Bastar district. The official district page gives its height as approximately 90 feet and its distance as about 40 km from Jagdalpur and 273 km from Raipur. It describes the waterfall as horseshoe-shaped and notes that its appearance changes with the season and water flow. The page recommends July to October for a dramatic monsoon view, but visitors should check local weather, access and safety notices before visiting.

title: Tirathgarh Waterfall — Kanger Valley
text: Tirathgarh Waterfall is within the Kanger Valley area of Bastar district. The official page places it about 35 km from Jagdalpur and describes water cascading down a height of around 300 feet. It is associated with the Kanger Valley landscape and is listed as a major natural attraction. The source gives October to April as a suitable period while also mentioning the rainy season; actual access and conditions vary with rainfall and official park rules.
category: tourism; waterfall; Kanger Valley National Park; nature

title: Kanger Valley National Park — Bastar
text: Kanger Valley National Park is described by the official Bastar district page as being about 34 km from Jagdalpur and having been declared a national park in 1982. The page highlights its mixed deciduous forests, including sal, teak and bamboo, as well as wildlife and bird diversity. Attractions associated with the park include Kotumsar, Kailash and Dandak caves and Tirathgarh Waterfall. Access to caves and park areas may be seasonal or regulated, so current visitor guidance should be checked.
category: tourism; national park; biodiversity; forests; wildlife

title: Kotumsar Cave — Bastar
text: Kotumsar Cave is a limestone cave in the Kanger Valley area near Jagdalpur. The official district page describes its underground formations and reports that the cave was studied after its discovery in 1951 by geographer Dr. Shankar Tiwari. The page includes geological and prehistoric-human claims that should not be treated as scientifically verified without consulting specialist sources. Cave access may be restricted during the monsoon or when conditions are unsafe.

title: Kailash Cave — Bastar
text: Kailash Cave is one of the limestone caves in Kanger Valley National Park. The official Bastar district tourist page says it was discovered on 22 March 1993 and describes stalactite and stalagmite formations resembling a Shivlinga. It reports a known length of about 1,000 feet and depth of about 120 feet. The page says the cave typically reopens from 16 October to 15 June and closes during the monsoon; visitors should confirm current dates and access arrangements with park authorities.
category: tourism; cave; limestone formations; natural heritage

title: About Bijapur District
text: Bijapur district is in the southern part of Chhattisgarh, India, and Bijapur town is its administrative headquarters. The district was previously part of Dantewada district. The official district page reports an area of approximately 8,529 square kilometres and describes a landscape with hills, forests, and the Indravati River along the southern limit. It identifies Bijapur, Bhairamgarh, Bhopalpatnam, and Usoor as four block divisions. The page also describes forest resources and palm-based products such as tar and sulphi. Treat this as a summary of the official page, not a verified current statistical profile.

title: Bijapur District Demography — Census 2011 and Statistical Handbook 2019–20
text: The official demography page states that its general information is based on Census 2011 and the District Statistical Handbook 2019–20. It gives the district formation date as 1 May 2007; area as 8,529 square kilometres; total population as 255,230; male population as 128,663; female population as 126,567; sex ratio as 984 females per 1,000 males; and population density as 39 people per square kilometre. It lists 699 villages, of which 581 are inhabited and 104 uninhabited, and four development blocks. The page reports literacy as 40.90%, while the homepage glance panel reports 41.58%; preserve this discrepancy and verify the source table before using the literacy value. These are historical/reference-period statistics, not current population estimates.

title: बीजापुर जिले की जनसांख्यिकी — जनगणना 2011 एवं सांख्यिकीय पुस्तिका 2019–20
text: बीजापुर जिले की आधिकारिक जनसांख्यिकी पृष्ठ के अनुसार, यह जानकारी जनगणना 2011 और जिला सांख्यिकीय पुस्तिका 2019–20 पर आधारित है। पृष्ठ पर जिला गठन की तारीख 1 मई 2007, क्षेत्रफल 8,529 वर्ग किलोमीटर, कुल जनसंख्या 2,55,230, पुरुष जनसंख्या 1,28,663 और महिला जनसंख्या 1,26,567 दी गई है। लिंगानुपात 1,000 पुरुषों पर 984 महिलाएँ और जनसंख्या घनत्व 39 व्यक्ति प्रति वर्ग किलोमीटर बताया गया है। पृष्ठ पर साक्षरता दर 40.90% है, जबकि जिले के मुखपृष्ठ पर 41.58% दी गई है। इस अंतर को सत्यापन के लिए चिह्नित करें। ये ऐतिहासिक संदर्भ-अवधि के आँकड़े हैं, वर्तमान जनसंख्या अनुमान नहीं।

title: History and Geography of Bijapur District
text: The official district history page describes Bijapur as the southernmost district area of Chhattisgarh, with Bijapur town as headquarters. title: Bhairamdev Historical and Religious Site, Bhairamgarh
text: The official places-of-interest page describes Bhairamdev in Bhairamgarh as a historical site associated with a Naga ruler named Narasimha Dev in the twelfth century. It mentions old temples and idols, a rock-carved Bhairava figure, a historical pond, archaeological remains, and a three-day Bhairamdev fair. The page states that the temple is about one kilometre east of the Bhairamgarh main road and mentions a site called Sita Hut and a stone gate known as Elephant Gate. title: Bhadrakali Temple near Bhopalpatnam
text: The official district tourism page describes Bhadrakali Temple as being on a hill along the Tarlaguda road, south of Bhopalpatnam, at a stated distance of about 18 km. title: Sakal Narayan Cave and Temple
text: The official district tourism page locates Sakal Narayan Cave on Govardhan mountain, reached via Cherrapalli village, and describes it as south of the Bhopalpatnam block headquarters. title: Nambi, Neelam Sarai, and Lankapalli Waterfalls
text: The official district tourism page describes Neelam Sarai as a stream or waterfall in Usoor block, reached from the Sodhi Para area after a walk over several hills. It describes Nambi waterfall near Nambi village, reached after Nadpalli, and gives an approximate drop of 300 feet. It also describes Lankapalli waterfall near Lankapalli village, west of Awapalli, and says it is locally called Bokta in Gondi. title: Dantewada Places of Interest — Official Tourism Overview
text: The official district tourism page describes Dantewada as part of the southern Bastar region and names Barsoor/Barsur, Bhadrakali and Dantewada among places of historical interest. It also mentions Bailadila, the Bacheli and Kirandul townships, Aakash Nagar and Kailash Nagar. The page says access to the mining-area peak at Aakash Nagar requires prior permission from NMDC, and describes buses and private taxis as transport options to Bacheli and Kirandul. Since access permissions, roads and transport can change, verify current arrangements locally before travel.

title: Barsur — Official District Tourism Description
text: The official Dantewada tourism page describes Barsur as a historic settlement associated with the Gangawanshi rulers and calls it a city of temples and ponds. The page mentions the Mama-Bhanjaa Temple, Chandraditya Temple, Battisa Temple, a large Ganesha statue and an old pond. It gives approximate directions as Barsur being north of Geedam and describes taxis from Geedam as a transport option. Historical claims and distances here reflect the district tourism page and should be cross-checked with heritage or archaeological sources before being treated as definitive.

title: Bailadila, Bacheli and Kirandul — Official Tourism Description
text: The official Dantewada tourism page describes Bailadila as a mountain range known for iron ore deposits and identifies Bacheli and Kirandul as townships associated with the industrial area. It mentions Aakash Nagar and Kailash Nagar as hilltop locations and states that access to the mining-area peak at Aakash Nagar requires prior permission from NMDC. These details are taken from the district tourism page and may be outdated; do not use them as confirmation of present-day mine access, visitor permissions, road status or operating conditions.

title: Dantewada Culture and Heritage — Official District Overview
text: The official district culture-and-heritage page discusses tribal communities, festivals known as Pandum, foodways, crafts, folk songs, dances and local dialects. It names communities including Muriyas/Dandami Mariyas or Gonds, Dorla and Halba, and describes crafts using clay, stone, bamboo and metals. The page lists examples of Pandum observances across months, including Vijja Pandum, Ama Pandum, Pane Pandum, Dela Pandum and Gadi Pandum. The page contains broad generalizations and some dated or potentially insensitive descriptions; use respectful wording, avoid treating any community as culturally uniform, and seek community-authored or locally reviewed sources before building detailed cultural answers.

title: About Sukma District
text: The official Sukma district portal describes Sukma as being at the southern tip of Chhattisgarh and says the district was carved out of Dantewada in 2012. The page reports that more than 85% of the population is Scheduled Tribe, around 65% of the area is forest-covered, population density is about 45 persons per square kilometre, and literacy is 29%. It identifies the Sabari River as a major river. These figures are portal-reported and should be checked against the demography page and the relevant Census/statistical reference before being presented as current.

title: History of Sukma District
text: The official history page says Sukma became a separate district on 16 January 2012. It states that the area was a sub-tehsil under Bastar in 1952, was upgraded to a tehsil in 1956, and that Konta tehsil was formed in 1960. It describes Sukma as having later been part of Dantewada district after Dantewada was separated from Bastar, before Sukma became a district in 2012. The page also includes traditional beliefs and a historical narrative about local settlement; these should be identified as beliefs or attributed accounts rather than established archaeological facts.

title: Sukma Demography — Census 2011 Reference
text: The official Sukma demography page labels its population data as provisional figures from the 2011 Census. It lists district formation date 16 January 2012; area 5,897.79 sq km; total population 270,821; male population 133,350; female population 137,471; Scheduled Tribe population share 85%; sex ratio 1,017 females per 1,000 males; population density 45 per sq km; literacy rate 29%; male literacy 49.69%; female literacy 23.33%; forest cover 65%; 2 revenue subdivisions; 3 tehsils; 7 RI circles; 113 patwari circles; 146 gram panchayats; 1 municipality; and 3 nagar panchayats. The page's total population differs from some commonly reported 2011 Census figures for the later district geography, so preserve the official page's attribution and validate boundary/reference-year compatibility before answering numerical questions.

title: Places of Interest in Sukma District

It places Dudma about 28 km from Sukma district headquarters and Tungal Dam about 3 km from the headquarters. The page describes Tungal Dam as a project intended to develop an eco-tourism centre, with infrastructure and activities reported in a historical account including an inauguration on 2 October 2015. It places Dornapal bridge about 37 km from the district headquarters and describes it as an important connection toward Odisha. Distances and facilities are from the district page and should be checked locally before travel.

title: Dudma Tourist Spot
text: The official Sukma tourist-place page describes Dudma as a nature-oriented tourist spot about 28 km from Sukma district headquarters. Its travel information lists Raipur's Swami Vivekananda International Airport at about 383 km, Jagdalpur railway station at about 93 km, and Pandri Bus Stop in Raipur at about 378 km. These are distances stated on the official page, not live route calculations; road conditions, transport availability and exact routing should be checked before travel.

title: Culture and Heritage — Injeram
text: The official Sukma culture-and-heritage page highlights Injeram, described as a village about 70 km from Sukma toward Konta and around 10 km before Konta along the national highway. The page reports that ancient sculptures and stone carvings depicting Hindu deities can be seen near the road, including a sculpture representing Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh on one stone. Its connection to the Ramayana period is presented as popular belief, not verified historical fact. The page itself suggests that further archaeological study would be useful.

title: How to Reach Sukma
text: The official Sukma transport page says daily bus services connect Sukma with Raipur and road links connect it with Jagdalpur, Dantewada, Malkangiri, Hyderabad and Vijayawada. It mentions interstate bus services to Hyderabad, Vijayawada and Rajahmundry, with National Highway 30 passing through the district. The page lists Dantewada and Jagdalpur as nearby railway-station options and Jagdalpur Airport as the nearest airport, giving an approximate distance of 100 km. Routes, schedules, airport services and distances can change; this is not live travel information.

title: Sukma District Survey Report 2026 — Profile and Geography
text: Source: District Survey Report for Sand Mining or River Bed Mining, Sukma, 2026, compiled by the Directorate of Geology and Mining, Regional Office Jagdalpur; PDF pages 3–4 and 16. The report gives district area as 5,897.79 km² and Census 2011 population as 270,821, density as 45 persons/km², and identifies the Sabari River as the principal river system. It names other drainage features including Phool Nadi, Malenjar, Baru, Gorli and Jhiram. The report describes hilly terrain, forest cover and rainfed agricultural areas. The report's general profile table lists 7 tehsils and 393 villages, which differs from counts on other district portal pages; retain as a report-specific figure pending reconciliation.

title: Sukma District Survey Report 2026 — Agriculture and Land Use
text: Source: Sukma District Survey Report 2026, PDF page 17. The report describes land use as predominantly forested and reports approximately 65% forest cover. Agriculture is mainly rainfed, with paddy as the principal crop. Other crops mentioned include kodo-kutki, maize, pigeon pea and sorghum in the Kharif season, and chickpea, peanuts and limited-area vegetables in the Rabi season. It also mentions minor forest produce, horticulture, animal husbandry and fisheries as livelihood-related activities, and notes departmental initiatives around millets, organic/natural farming, micro-irrigation and mechanization. These are report descriptions and should not be interpreted as measured current production totals.

title: Sukma District Survey Report 2026 — Sand Mining Overview
text: Source: Sukma District Survey Report 2026, PDF pages 10–12 and 16. The report identifies the Sabari River and tributaries, along with the Malger and Baro rivers, as sand-bearing river systems. It states that one sand mine at Gram Panchayat Puspal was operational and that two additional sand mines in the Sukma and Konta areas on the Sabari had been allotted by e-auction under Chhattisgarh Minor Mineral (Ordinary Sand) Rules, 2025, subject to environmental clearance and other permissions. The report lists sand royalty receipts of Rs 370,600 in FY 2022–23, Rs 19,550 in FY 2023–24, Rs 0 in FY 2024–25 and Rs 105,000 in FY 2025–26, totaling Rs 495,150. Treat these as figures reported in the 2026 survey report; mining operations and clearances can change.

title: Sukma District Statistical Report 2016–17: Subject coverage and extraction status
text: The official 107-page Sukma District Statistical Report 2016–17 is a broad statistical compendium. Its table of contents covers geographic and administrative structure; population, literacy and working population; agriculture and allied services; forest statistics; mining and quarrying; industry and employment; electricity; education; health and public health; drinking water and roads; public distribution; banking; transport and communications; crime and justice; local bodies; revenue and finance; newspapers and vital registration. The current RAG collection has extracted a small set of topic summaries and selected figures from the PDF text layer. It has not yet exhaustively extracted all 107 pages or manually verified all tables, so this is a source inventory rather than a claim of complete report coverage.

title: A brief introduction to District Sukma (2017): historical administrative profile
text: The district portal lists a document titled “A brief introduction to District Sukma,” dated 12 July 2017, with a PDF size of approximately 530 KB. The linked PDF is a short historical district profile covering administrative units, population and local institutions, education and health facilities, forest circles, irrigation projects, markets, revenue villages, land area and tourist sites. Some figures in the legacy document differ from current portal pages and the later 2016–17 statistical report. Preserve it as a dated historical source and do not merge its numbers with current values without checking reference year and administrative boundaries. The PDF text extraction is legacy Hindi OCR and needs manual review for individual figures.

title: Sukma Potential Linked Credit Plan 2016–17: Agro-climatic profile and rainfall
text: A NABARD Potential Linked Credit Plan (PLP) 2016–17 district profile describes Sukma as part of Zone VIII — Eastern Plateau and Hills (Bastar Plateau Region), with predominantly red sandy loam and red soils. It reports a total geographical area of 5,635.79 km² and normal rainfall of 1,690 mm. Actual rainfall shown for 2012–13, 2013–14 and 2014–15 is 2,068 mm, 1,758 mm and 1,466 mm respectively. These are historical planning-profile values, not current rainfall or climate normals validated for present use.

title: Sukma Potential Linked Credit Plan 2016–17: Land use and cropping
text: The NABARD PLP 2016–17 district profile lists total reported area as 563,579 hectares. It gives forest land as 210,814 ha; area not available for cultivation 22,702 ha; permanent pasture and grazing land 26,811 ha; cultivable wasteland 47,355 ha; current fallow 6,542 ha; other fallow 17,671 ha; net sown area 96,348 ha; gross cropped area 97,389 ha; and area cultivated more than once 1,041 ha. The reported cropping intensity is 105%. These are historical figures copied from the plan profile; category totals and the underlying source year should be checked before using them as current land-use statistics.

title: Sukma Potential Linked Credit Plan 2016–17: Distribution of agricultural landholdings
text: The NABARD PLP 2016–17 profile reports 32,327 agricultural holdings in Sukma. It classifies 6,245 holdings (19%) as up to 1 hectare, 12,974 holdings (40%) as more than 1 and up to 2 hectares, and 13,108 holdings (41%) as above 2 hectares. The report’s table gives corresponding area shares as 10%, 13% and 77%. These are historical profile values and the area/holding classification should be validated against the original table before use in quantitative analysis.

title: Sukma Potential Linked Credit Plan 2016–17: Worker profile
text: The NABARD PLP 2016–17 district profile gives an approximate worker profile, in thousands: 32 cultivators, of whom 19 are small/marginal farmers; 10 agricultural labourers; 4 workers in household industries; 4 workers engaged in allied agro-activities; and 45 other workers. The source presents these as rounded figures in a district planning profile, not a current labour-force estimate. Do not combine these rounded figures with later employment data without preserving the reference year and definitions.

title: Sukma Potential Linked Credit Plan 2016–17: Demographic profile
text: The NABARD PLP 2016–17 profile presents rounded demographic indicators for Sukma, in thousands: population 250, male population 124, female population 126, rural population 223 and urban population 17. It reports Scheduled Caste population of 11 thousand, Scheduled Tribe population of 174 thousand, and literate population of 91 thousand (62 thousand male and 29 thousand female). These are rounded historical profile values, likely based on Census-era statistics; use exact Census tables for precise calculations and retain this source as a dated secondary planning summary.

title: Sukma Potential Linked Credit Plan 2016–17: Village and health infrastructure
text: The NABARD PLP 2016–17 district profile lists 379 inhabited villages and 132 panchayats. It reports 259 villages electrified, 39 villages with post offices, 858 Anganwadis, 12 Primary Health Centres, 81 Primary Health Sub-Centres and 3 hospitals. These figures differ from some other official district pages and later administrative listings. Treat them as historical planning-profile figures, preserve their source and year, and verify definitions and coverage before using them to answer present-day service-availability questions.

title: Sukma Health Department: Health facility counts by block
text: The official Sukma Health page lists 3 Community Health Centres, 15 Primary Health Centres and 95 Sub Health Centres across the district. Its block table gives Sukma: 0 CHCs, 3 PHCs, 21 sub-health centres; Chindgarh: 1 CHC, 6 PHCs, 39 sub-health centres; Konta: 2 CHCs, 6 PHCs, 35 sub-health centres. The same page says District Hospital Sukma began operating at Kumharras in 2016 as a 100-bed hospital and that the Mother and Child Health building was inaugurated in November 2019. These are page-reported infrastructure details; current operational status and bed availability are not independently verified. This count differs from older statistical sources and should be retained with the source and collection date.

title: Sukma Agriculture Department: Official department page inventory
text: The official district portal provides a dedicated Agriculture department page. This record preserves the page as an authoritative starting point for agriculture-related district information, but the page content available during this collection pass did not expose enough substantive text to create a reliable summary of current schemes, crop production, input distribution or farmer services. Use the linked page for further extraction and do not treat this metadata record itself as evidence of particular schemes or current agricultural statistics.

title: Sukma land survey and resurvey status: Government of India DILRMP dashboard
text: The Department of Land Resources' DILRMP survey/resurvey dashboard reports a total mapped area of 1,895.51 km² for Sukma in its displayed survey-status table, with 1,850.88 km² surveyed (97.65%), 30.98 km² rural area and 13.65 km² urban area; it lists 282 villages in the survey-status table. These fields describe the programme's survey coverage and are not equivalent to the district's full geographical area or total village count. The dashboard includes tehsil entries such as Chhindgarh, Dornapal, Gadiras, Jagargunda, Konta, Sukma and Tongpal. Capture the dashboard date and definitions before using these numbers; do not confuse survey coverage with district area.

title: Sukma watershed baseline survey: Land classification and cropped area
text: The Government of India's WDC-PMKSY baseline survey dashboard displays two Sukma watershed projects, SUKMA-WDC-1/2021-22 and SUKMA-WDC-2/2021-22. Combined project area is shown as 13,166 hectares, plot area as 14,267.24 hectares, net sown area as 739.57 hectares, gross cropped area as 749.81 hectares, and total value of output as ₹295.36 lakh. The dashboard's land classification columns include cultivable wasteland, degraded land, rainfed, forest land and others. These values apply to the listed watershed project areas, not to the whole district; the report itself warns that total income is the total value of output.

title: Sukma Bank BC List: Official district document inventory
text: The Sukma district Documents page lists a document titled “Sukma Bank BC List,” dated 20 May 2022, with a listed size of 403 KB. This record captures document metadata only. The file contents have not been extracted in this pass, so no names, banking correspondents, contact details, service locations or current operating status should be inferred from this record. If extracted later, treat it as a dated directory and avoid presenting it as a current list without validation.

title: Sukma District Survey Report 2025: Official document metadata
text: The official Sukma portal lists a District Survey Report dated 27 November 2025, available as a 4 MB PDF. A separate 2026 District Survey Report is also listed on the portal, dated 15 October 2026. This record captures the 2025 report's title/date/availability as source metadata; it does not represent a full extraction of the 2025 PDF. For questions about sand mining, geology, river beds or environmental clearances, extract and validate the report's actual content and distinguish it from the 2026 report.

title: Sukma District Survey Report 2025: Geographic and administrative profile
text: The Sukma District Survey Report 2025 was prepared by the Directorate of Geology and Mining, Chhattisgarh, Regional Office Jagdalpur, and updated under instructions dated 15 September 2025. The PDF is 39 pages. Its general profile reports district area 5,897.79 km², coordinates 17°46′55″–18°46′26″ N and 80°55′20″–81°57′30″ E, seven tehsils (Sukma, Konta, Chhindgarh, Gadiras, Jagargunda, Tongpal and Dornapal), 146 panchayats and 393 villages, Census 2011 population 270,821, density 45 persons/km², and forest area 290,652.713 hectares. The report's 393-village and 146-panchayat figures differ from other district portal pages; preserve the report-specific values and verify administrative definitions before resolving conflicts.

title: Sukma District Survey Report 2025: Geology and mineral resources
text: The 2025 District Survey Report describes rock units including the Eastern Ghat Supergroup, Bengpal Group, Dongargarh granite, Abujhmar Group and Sabri Group, with lithologies such as granulite, charnockite, gneiss, schist, amphibolite, quartzite, granite, sandstone, limestone, shale and alluvium. It identifies reported economic mineral occurrences primarily as tin in the Kikirpal area and corundum in the Nagaras area. It also mentions building materials such as aggregate, sand, murum, ordinary stone and brick clay. These are report-referenced geological occurrences and do not imply that every material is currently being mined or commercially available.

title: Sukma District Survey Report 2025: Mining leases and royalty figures
text: The report's general profile lists one major-mineral mining lease covering 11.541 hectares, two minor-mineral quarry leases covering 5.389 hectares, and nine notified sand leases covering 34.513 hectares. It reports major-mineral royalty/revenue of ₹102,173 for 2020–25 and minor-mineral revenue of ₹23,213,078 for the same period in the profile table. Other royalty tables in the PDF show year-by-year values and some OCR/table-layout inconsistencies, so the aggregate figures should be treated as report-specific and cross-checked against the original table before numerical analysis. Lease counts and areas are as stated in the 2025 report, not a live lease register.

title: Sukma District Survey Report 2025: Sand production and royalty, FY 2020–21 to 2024–25
text: The sand production table in the 2025 District Survey Report gives annual production and royalty as follows: FY 2020–21, 51,200 m³ and ₹2,560,000; FY 2021–22, 26,492 m³ and ₹1,324,600; FY 2022–23, 7,412 m³ and ₹370,600; FY 2023–24, 391 m³ and ₹19,550; FY 2024–25, 0 m³ and ₹0. The report totals 85,495 m³ and ₹4,274,750 across these five years. These values are directly represented in the PDF text layer, but validate the original table image before production use. They are historical report figures, not a statement about current sand availability or legal extraction status.

title: Sukma District Survey Report 2025: Forest cover, agriculture and irrigation
text: The 2025 report describes approximately 65% of Sukma district as forest-covered, with Sal and Sagaun named as principal tree types. It characterizes agriculture as predominantly rain-fed and paddy as the principal crop. Other crops mentioned include kodo-kutki, maize, pigeon pea, sorghum, chickpea, peanuts and vegetables; fruit crops mentioned include mango, guava, papaya, cashew, lemon and banana. The report states that only about 1% of net sown area has irrigation facilities and mentions initiatives promoting millet, organic and natural farming, micro-irrigation and mechanization. These are statements in the district survey report; program implementation and current crop statistics are not independently verified here.

title: Sukma District Survey Report 2025: River system and sand replenishment study
text: The report identifies the Sabari/Sabri as a principal river flowing through the district and names the Phool Nadi and Malenjar/Malanger among other rivers or streams. It places Sukma in the Indravati Basin and states that a sand replenishment study had not been conducted for the Sabari River and its tributaries, noting the need for such a study. The report includes sections on river drainage, sediment deposition, rainfall, groundwater levels and geohydrology, but much of the rainfall and water-level information is presented in maps or scanned tables that were not numerically transcribed in this record. Do not infer current water levels or sand replenishment rates from this summary.

title: Animal Husbandry and Livestock Statistics in Sukma
text: The official Sukma district Animal Husbandry page provides livestock and poultry counts, but the page was last updated on 22 December 2018, so the figures must be treated as historical and not as current livestock estimates. It lists cattle as 268,013; buffaloes 41,738; goats 106,626; sheep 5,403; swine 55,423; and other animals 39, with a stated total livestock count of 477,242 and total poultry of 289,244. The page lists six veterinary hospitals, 13 veterinary dispensaries, and one mobile hospital unit for the district. The category values and totals should be checked against the underlying livestock census because the source uses the label “Catal” for cattle and does not clearly state the enumeration year.

title: School Inventory and Education Challenges in Sukma
text: The official Sukma district Education page describes challenges including disparities in school quality and shortages of specialist teachers in higher grades, including mathematics, physics, chemistry and English. It discusses residential Ashram Shalas for children from remote villages and POTA Cabin Ashrams for students who have dropped out. Its school-at-a-glance table lists 1,054 schools across three blocks: Chhindgarh 405, Konta 375 and Sukma 274. The table reports 61 clusters in total. These figures are a snapshot from the district portal, whose displayed page was last updated on 29 September 2026; they should not be assumed to be a live school count. The abbreviated school-type columns are retained on the source page and need careful interpretation before using individual category totals.

title: आदिवासी कल्याण: छात्रावास, आश्रम और छात्रवृत्ति योजनाएँ
text: सुकमा जिला प्रशासन के आदिवासी कल्याण पृष्ठ पर छात्रावासों और आश्रमों की स्वीकृत संख्या तथा सीटों का विवरण दिया गया है। पृष्ठ की तालिका में विभिन्न श्रेणियों के लिए कुल 150 संस्थाएँ और 12,290 स्वीकृत सीटें बताई गई हैं; इसमें अनुसूचित जनजाति छात्रावास, प्राथमिक और माध्यमिक आश्रम, पिछड़ा वर्ग छात्रावास, कन्या शिक्षा परिसर और एकलव्य आदर्श आवासीय विद्यालय शामिल हैं। पृष्ठ पर छात्रवृत्ति, भोजन सहायता, पोस्ट-मैट्रिक छात्रवृत्ति और विशेष कोचिंग जैसी योजनाओं का भी वर्णन है। ये संख्याएँ पृष्ठ पर उपलब्ध प्रशासनिक स्नैपशॉट हैं; पृष्ठ पर स्पष्ट अद्यतन तिथि नहीं दिखती और तालिका के कुछ कॉलम/पंक्तियों का OCR या स्वरूपण अस्पष्ट है। वर्तमान पात्रता, राशि और सीट उपलब्धता के लिए नवीनतम विभागीय आदेश की पुष्टि आवश्यक है।

title: Tribal Welfare: Residential Institutions and Scholarships in Sukma
text: The official district Tribal Welfare page lists residential institutions and approved seats across several categories, including pre-matric and post-matric Scheduled Tribe hostels, primary and middle-level ashrams, a Backward Class post-matric hostel, a girls’ education complex, Eklavya Model Residential Schools and non-government ashram schools. Its table gives a stated total of 150 institutions and 12,290 approved seats, but the layout of some rows is ambiguous and the page does not show a clear last-updated date. The page also describes scholarship support, food assistance for post-matric hostel students, post-matric scholarships, minority scholarships and special coaching for students in classes 8, 10 and 12. Amounts and eligibility rules on the page may be dated; users should confirm them with the current department notification before relying on them.

title: सुकमा जिला परिचय पुस्तिका (2017): प्रशासनिक और सार्वजनिक सेवाओं का ऐतिहासिक स्नैपशॉट
text: सुकमा जिला प्रशासन की 12 जुलाई 2017 की “A brief introduction to District Sukma” पुस्तिका छह पृष्ठों की हिंदी PDF है। उपलब्ध PDF टेक्स्ट में 2011 जनगणना-आधारित स्थानीय निकाय/क्षेत्रवार जनसंख्या तालिकाएँ, तीन तहसीलों (कोंटा, सुकमा और छिंदगढ़) का प्रशासनिक संदर्भ, शिक्षा और स्वास्थ्य संस्थानों की तालिकाएँ, वन परिक्षेत्र, सिंचाई परियोजनाएँ, आंगनवाड़ी/महिला एवं बाल विकास, बाजार और राजस्व ग्रामों की जानकारी शामिल है। PDF का टेक्स्ट पुराने हिंदी फॉन्ट/OCR के कारण आंशिक रूप से विकृत है; इसलिए इस रिकॉर्ड में केवल विषय-सूची और ऐतिहासिक संदर्भ सुरक्षित किया गया है, न कि अस्पष्ट तालिकाओं के संख्यात्मक मान। इसे वर्तमान प्रशासनिक संरचना या वर्तमान सेवा उपलब्धता का प्रमाण न माना जाए।

title: Sukma District Department Pages: Content Coverage and Retrieval Limits
text: The official Sukma portal has dedicated pages for Mining, Revenue, and Women and Child Development, but the current English pages opened during collection contain little or no substantive explanatory text beyond the department heading, site navigation, and ownership information. The Mining page was last updated on 18 June 2020, the Revenue page on 20 January 2026, and the Women and Child Development page on 2 September 2026. These pages are useful as official source endpoints but should not be indexed as if they explain schemes, procedures, or current services. For WCD scheme details, individual dated notices may provide specific information; those notices must be indexed with their own dates and should not be generalized into current policy without checking status.

title: Raipur DCHB 2011: district-wide total workers
text: The Census of India 2011 Raipur District Census Handbook Part B search-indexed table reports 1,757,664 total workers for the historical Raipur district geography: 1,099,964 males and 657,700 females. It breaks this down into 1,215,693 rural workers and 541,971 urban workers. This is the 2011 district geography in the handbook, which predates later district bifurcations; do not equate it with the present Raipur district without geographic reconciliation.
quality_flag: Historical geography; district boundaries later changed. Verify directly against PDF before production.

title: Raipur DCHB 2011: main workers and marginal workers
text: The indexed Census 2011 handbook table reports 1,259,138 main workers (879,956 males; 379,182 females) and 498,526 marginal workers (220,008 males; 278,518 females) for the historical Raipur district. Main and marginal worker figures are separate Census categories and should not be treated as employment estimates for the current district.
quality_flag: Historical boundary; direct PDF validation recommended.

title: Raipur DCHB 2011: worker category distribution
text: The indexed Census 2011 handbook reports, for the historical Raipur district, 303,519 main workers classified as cultivators, 354,429 as agricultural labourers, 27,637 in household industry, and 573,553 as other workers. These categories describe the handbook's historical district boundary and Census definitions, not the current district's labour market.
quality_flag: Historical geography and Census categories; check totals against table before production.

title: Raipur DCHB 2011: non-workers
text: The indexed Census 2011 handbook table reports 2,306,208 non-workers in the historical Raipur district: 948,222 males and 1,357,986 females. It reports 1,364,890 rural non-workers and 941,318 urban non-workers. These numbers use the old district geography and should not be applied to current Raipur district boundaries.
quality_flag: Historical boundary; direct PDF validation recommended.

title: Raipur DCHB 2011: Simga CD block workers
text: The indexed Census 2011 handbook reports 89,016 total workers in Simga CD block (50,193 males; 38,823 females), including 54,632 main workers and 34,384 marginal workers. The source table labels Simga as a CD block under the historical Raipur district. Confirm current administrative mapping before using the record for today's district boundaries.
quality_flag: Historical CD block geography; check present district assignment.

title: Raipur DCHB 2011: Simga block village Hirmi
text: The indexed Census 2011 handbook includes Hirmi (Census Town) under Simga CD block. The available search-indexed excerpt indicates a population of 1,833 (1,324 males and 509 females). Other nearby worker and non-worker figures in the snippet cannot be confidently assigned to the Hirmi row because the table columns and adjacent rows are interleaved in the search result; they are intentionally excluded pending direct PDF inspection.
quality_flag: Only population figures retained from snippet; row alignment for other metrics is ambiguous and requires direct PDF check.

title: Raipur DCHB 2011: Scheduled Tribe PCA district summary
text: A separate Scheduled Tribe Primary Census Abstract table in the indexed official handbook reports 241,622 Scheduled Tribe non-workers in the historical Raipur district (104,704 males; 136,918 females), with 199,682 rural and 41,940 urban. The same indexed rows show 5,262 Scheduled Tribe workers classified as other workers (2,995 males; 2,267 females). This is a subset/category-specific table, not the total district population.
quality_flag: Category/table context must be retained; verify table layout in PDF.

title: Raipur DCHB 2011: village-level PCA schema
text: The official Raipur District Census Handbook Part B contains a village-level Primary Census Abstract with fields including location code, village name, population, population aged 0–6, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe population, literates, illiterates, total workers, main workers and marginal workers. The Census catalogue identifies a separate PCA-TV spreadsheet for Raipur with town-, village- and ward-level indicators. The spreadsheet itself was not downloaded or parsed in this extraction run.
quality_flag: Data dictionary/source pointer; XLSX not imported.

title: Raipur district historical-boundary warning
text: The official 2011 District Census Handbook describes the historical Raipur district and includes CD blocks and places such as Simga, Bhatapara and Balodabazar in its tables. Since several districts were subsequently created from the former Raipur district, the handbook's district-wide totals are not interchangeable with figures for today's Raipur district. All extracted records from this handbook must carry Census year 2011 and historical-boundary metadata.
quality_flag: Boundary warning: reconcile using location codes and current district map before retrieval.

title: Raipur Census source details and coverage
text: The Census of India catalogue lists the 2011 District Census Handbook Part XII B for Raipur, published in 2014 by the Directorate of Census Operations, Chhattisgarh. It describes village-, town- and ward-level Primary Census Abstract data and includes PDF, town-amenities XLSX, village-amenities XLSX and inset tables. This record documents source coverage; it is not a substitute for parsing the complete files.
quality_flag: Source metadata only.
